scope: model_compound_actual_failure_recheck; supplied full current source/tests and explicitly labeled integration diff if present

findings.title: Generic exception handler swallows and re-raises as LLMOutcomeUnknown any pre-transport failure, including grant/scope validation errors other than CapabilityDenied
findings.issue: complete_with_receipt only re-raises CapabilityDenied unchanged; every other exception raised inside execute_reserved_groups (e.g. a local scope/binding validation StorageError before any I/O, or a ScopePreparationUnknown from the compound wrapper) is converted into LLMOutcomeUnknown with external_call_attempted possibly false and retry_allowed=False. That is conservative for retry, but it loses typed preparation/invalid input classification and can label a never-attempted call as an unknown provider outcome with a durable model_attempt fence already created, permanently fencing a task that never reached the transport.
findings.fix: Distinguish pre-transport failures (no I/O occurred) from transport outcomes: re-raise ScopePreparationUnknown/StorageError validation errors unchanged, and only wrap failures where http_attempted is true into LLMOutcomeUnknown. Keep the ModelResponseInvalid fast path as-is.

findings.title: usage_observer failure on successful call raises and is not marked unconfirmed, yet receipt already claims accepted usage
findings.issue: After a successful transport the usage_observer call is not wrapped; if it raises (the failure mode the #60 patch guards on the error path) the exception propagates raw while the durable operations are already settled as accepted and the logical model_attempt fence is created. Callers see a raw accounting error with no receipt/refs, indistinguishable from a local failure, and cannot tell that the model call actually succeeded and must not be retried.
findings.fix: Wrap the success-path observer call and attach operation_refs/attempt_ref with accounting_status='unconfirmed' (non-retryable) rather than raising raw, mirroring the error path behavior.

findings.title: ModelAttemptAlreadyRecorded/ModelResponseInvalid error attribute injection is untyped and mutable
findings.issue: operation_refs/attempt_ref/retry_allowed/accounting_status are set as ad-hoc attributes on ModelResponseInvalid (frozen dataclass instance but not the attribute set) and on LLMOutcomeUnknown; nothing guarantees accounting_status exists for all downstream consumers, and the same mutable instance is re-raised with attributes added after construction. This is brittle but does not currently turn unknown into allow.
findings.fix: Define explicit typed exception classes carrying operation_refs, attempt_ref, retry_allowed and accounting_status at construction.

findings.title: ModelEndpoint does not validate the endpoint URL path or reject whitespace-only model/token edge cases consistently
findings.issue: Validation allows any path and any token string without spaces/newlines, and permits an empty token for synthetic_http only; for non-synthetic endpoints it requires a non-empty token but does not reject tokens containing other control characters. This is bounded and does not cause an allow escalation.
findings.fix: Reject control characters in token and enforce a bounded, allowlisted path shape for the endpoint.

not_verified: Behavior of llm/client LLMOutcomeUnknown and prm/runtime/composition callers is not in the packet; assertions about their handling of injected attributes/unknowns are unverified.
Source for registry.execute_reserved_groups wrapping behavior in this exact revision is present but the documented 8 corrected HTTP tests were not re-run by this review.
The dependency/lineage lock path (deletion.lineage_lock, postgres store transactions) is not in the packet; concurrency under real Postgres locking was not verified.
Any code outside the five supplied files (e.g. how accounting_status is consumed in reporting) is omitted and not reviewed.
findings.summary: The #60 accounting-masking defect appears correctly addressed: checked_transport now retains only a positively observed ModelResponseInvalid before the compound wrapper, and the error path re-raises that typed non-retryable failure with fence refs even if the usage observer fails, while other transport failures remain LLMOutcomeUnknown with conservative unknown spend and no blind retry/refund. The known-invalid + failed-accounting test path is consistent with the described fix and preserves the one-use fence. Remaining P1s are adjacent correctness gaps: any non-CapabilityDenied pre-transport error is mislabeled as an unknown provider outcome after a durable fence is created, and a success-path usage_observer failure propagates raw despite the call having succeeded and settled as accepted; both are fail-closed for retry but degrade classification and accounting honesty, so fix before ship.
